We study pairwise disjoint sets of denominators in a common interval whose reciprocal sums are prescribed rational numbers. Put $L=\log N$ and $U=\log L$. For targets in a fixed compact subinterval of $(1/d,\infty)$ satisfying a common denominator condition, our sufficient and necessary bounds give the same first two terms in the loss from the harmonic mass of $[d,N]$, namely $U^2/(2L)+U\log U/L$. The construction also bounds the number of terms in each group. For unit targets, let $\mathfrak C_N$ be the maximum reciprocal mass compatible with the zero-residue conditions at the primes above $\sqrt N$. For all but $O(X^{11/12})$ integers $N\le X$, both the maximum number of disjoint unit sums and the largest integer representable by a single subset are equal to $\lfloor\mathfrak C_N\rfloor$. If $X_j$ denotes either the least height permitting $j$ disjoint unit sums or the least height permitting one representation of $j$, then \[ \log X_j=j-\gamma+\frac{(\log j)^2}{2j} +\frac{\log j\,\log\log j}{j} +O\!\left(\frac{\log j\,\log\log\log j}{j}\right). \]

entry.title: The generalized Segal conjecture and the coalgebraic Frobenius
entry.summary: author: Thomas Nikolaus; abstract: algebraic k-theor
entry.content:
author: Thomas Nikolaus; abstract: algebraic k-theor

Thomas Nikolaus

We prove the generalized Segal conjecture, extending work of Bergsaker and Rognes and confirming a conjecture by the author: for every finite group $G$ and every bounded-below spectrum $X$, the Hill--Hopkins--Ravenel norm $N_e^G X$ becomes Borel-complete after completion at the augmentation ideal of the Burnside ring. Equivalently, for every non-trivial finite $p$-group $G$, the proper Tate diagonal $X\to(X^{\otimes G})^{\varphi G}$ is a $p$-completion. The proof reduces to the case $X=\Fp$, established by Bergsaker and Rognes, and removes the finiteness hypotheses from their theorem by abstract manipulations. As an application of this result, we refine the coalgebraic Frobenius to an oriented circle action (i.e. an action of the monoidal category $B\mathbb N$) on the category of bounded-below, $p$-complete $\mathbb{E}_\infty$-coalgebras, confirming another conjecture by the author. The construction is based on Yuan's approach to Frobenius actions via partial algebraic $K$-theory.

entry.title: Equivariant $K$-homology of affine Grassmannians of orthogonal groups
entry.content:
title: equivariant

Koushik Brahma, Takeshi Ikeda, Mark Shimozono

We construct explicit symmetric-function realizations of the torus-equivariant $K$-homology of affine Grassmannians of types B and D. More precisely, we realize the extended $K$-theoretic Peterson algebras as subalgebras of a completed ring of equivariant symmetric functions and identify their Schubert classes in terms of symmetric functions. We introduce two new families of equivariant symmetric functions for each of types B and D and prove that these functions represent the classes of the structure sheaves of Schubert varieties and the ideal sheaves of their boundaries, respectively. We establish several fundamental properties of these functions, including translation factorization formulas and explicit expressions for the classes indexed by small affine Grassmannian elements. In type D, we further describe the action of the affine Dynkin diagram automorphism interchanging the two spin nodes and show how it intertwines the Schubert bases with a nontrivial transformation of the equivariant parameters.

entry.title: Higher rewriting for strong linearly distributive coherence
entry.content:
abstract: higher categor

Max Demirdilek, Christian Reiher, Christoph Schweigert

Rewriting is a computational method to solve word problems: deciding whether two compound expressions, or words, are equivalent with respect to a set of identities. Higher rewriting generalizes rewriting to higher-dimensional words, or cells, in higher categories. Following Guiraud and Malbos, we use higher rewriting to generalize Mac Lane's coherence theorem. Our result concerns strong linearly distributive categories: categories equipped with two unital tensor products related by invertible distributors. We show that in a strong linearly distributive category every formal diagram commutes.

entry.title: $E_d$-Enhancements of $L_\infty$-Algebras Associated to Secondary Polytopes
entry.content:
Longfei Li

We study $E_d$-enhancements of the geometric $L_\infty$-algebras associated to secondary polytopes of finite configurations in $\mathbb R^d$, $d\geq2$. We construct an action of the semialgebraic chains of the Fulton--MacPherson operad on the shifted algebra $B_A=\mathfrak g_A[1-d]$ when $|A|\leq3d$. The action recovers the prescribed higher Lie operations on fundamental chains. The construction is obtained from a general extension theorem for weighted shifted $L_\infty$-algebras, using reflection to control relative cohomology obstructions. For $|A|\leq3d-1$, the resulting reflection-compatible integration actions are homotopic relative to their shifted Lie structure. We also give an abstract enhancement without a cardinality bound, direct formulas for circuits, and explicit operations for convex pentagons and hexagons.

Andrzej T. Karolak

The deleted square of a topological space is a subspace of the Cartesian product of this space with itself, obtained by removing the diagonal. Conjecturally, the deleted square of a cone over a graph has the homotopy type of a wedge sum of spheres of dimensions at most 3. We propose a geometric construction that is a key motivation for the conjecture and provides a major step towards its proof, while yielding direct results on deleted squares of certain families of graphs.

entry.title: Explicit covers and rigid obstructions for simplicial complexity: from spheres to surfaces
entry.content:
M. Perez, J. Flores

The strict simplicial complexity $SC_{\rm strict}(K)$, Gonz\'alez's simplicial complexity at subdivision level zero, is one less than the least number of contiguity domains covering the ordered product $K\times K$. We bound it from both sides. For upper bounds, every product of two vertex stars is a domain, which gives $SC_{\rm strict}(K)\le\rho(K)-1$ for an exactly computable set-cover number $\rho(K)$; the bound is sharp on every even-dimensional simplex boundary. A GPU annealer that evolves whole systems of contiguity chains finds three-domain covers of $\partial\Delta^3,\dots,\partial\Delta^7$ and of the cube boundary. Seeded by star covers, it descends from $24$ to $5$ domains on the icosahedron boundary, and an exact SAT completion of its stalled state gives $SC_{\rm strict}\le3$ there. For lower bounds, a subcomplex of $K\times K$ is rigid if its two projections are joined by no contiguity chain of any length; $k$ domains can cover $K\times K$ only if $k$ classes of facets avoid every rigid subcomplex, a finite SAT problem. Rigid subcomplexes arise from hollow triangles over essential empty triangles and, on complexes without dominated vertices, from the graph of every order-preserving simplicial self-map other than the identity. The resultingchain-length-free bounds give $SC_{\rm strict}(\partial\Delta^{n+1})=2>1=TC(S^n)$ for $n=3,5,7,9$, $SC_{\rm strict}=2>1$ for the five-vertex M\"obius band, $SC_{\rm strict}\ge3>2$ for the seven-vertex torus, and $4\le SC_{\rm strict}\le5$ and $4\le SC_{\rm strict}\le6$ for two triangulations of $\mathbb{RP}^2$. They also sort the annealer's stalls: on these two triangulations of $\mathbb{RP}^2$, the Klein bottle and $\partial\Delta^4$, almost every uncovered facet closes a rigid subcomplex in every domain, while the icosahedron stall was a search failure.

entry.title: Face posets, local weight matroids and Betti numbers of torus actions
entry.content:
David Mikheev

Let a compact torus act on a closed manifold $X$ with isolated fixed points. The face poset $S(X)$ of the action is covered by the lattices of flats of the linear matroids of tangent weights at the fixed points. We study how much of the cohomology of $X$ these combinatorial data see. Local equivariant cohomology. The group $H^*_T(X, X\setminus pt)$, embedded in $H^*_T(pt)$ by restriction, is the principal ideal generated by the product of the tangent weights. It determines the weights up to scalars, with multiplicities, and hence the local lattice $S(X)_{\geq pt}$. Local matroids do not suffice. Two connected regular semisimple Hessenberg varieties in $\mathrm{Fl}(\mathbb{C}^5)$, with torus actions of complexity one, have isomorphic weight matroids at all fixed points, and hence the same Chow rings, Orlik–Solomon algebras and Kazhdan–Lusztig polynomials there, but different Betti numbers. The face poset determines the Betti numbers of every regular semisimple Hessenberg variety of type A, full or partial, and of the isospectral manifolds of Ayzenberg and Buchstaber. The reason is rigidity: the cluster-permutohedron $\mathrm{Cl}_\Gamma$ determines the graph $\Gamma$, by an elementary argument that recovers the vertices of $\Gamma$ from stars of edges. Simply-laced types. The same holds for regular semisimple Hessenberg varieties of types A, D and E: the face poset determines the Weyl group together with the lines spanned by the roots of the Hessenberg ideal, up to isometry. A formula. The Poincaré polynomial is a sum over the face poset, $P_X(q)=\sum_{\sigma\in S(X)}(q-1)^{\mathrm{rk}\,\sigma}e_\sigma(q)$, in which $e_\sigma$ is a sum of Tutte polynomials of the matroids of weights that are negative on a generic circle. For toric manifolds this is the $h$-vector formula.

entry.title: Graded Monoidal Categories and Internalization
entry.content:
Bryce Goldman

In stable homotopy theory, there are a variety of ways to construct a point-set level smash product of spectra, each with its own advantages and limitations. These constructions often involve internalizing some graded external product. In this paper, we aim to formalize this process through a general categorical framework, providing a common language for these constructions. We propose a general theory for internalizing a graded monoidal product, investigate its 2-categorical properties, and use this framework to recover both Day convolution and the smash product of $S$-modules.

entry.title: The pentagonal tensor and the fourth obstruction to formality
entry.content:
Chaoshun Yang, Xiugui Liu

Let \(A\) be a connected graded commutative differential graded algebra over \(\mathbb Q\) whose cohomology is a finite-dimensional Poincar\'e duality algebra of formal dimension \(N\ge2\). Assuming that its Bianchi-Massey tensor vanishes, we prove that the normalized pentagonal tensor of Nagy and Nordstr\"om, in [preprint (2021), arXiv:2105.13660], vanishes if and only if the fourth Harrison obstruction vanishes after eliminating the third operation. This gives a fourth-order counterpart to the third-order comparison of Fiorenza and L\^e, in [Ann. Sc. Norm. Super. Pisa Cl. Sci. (5), published online 7 March 2025], and answers the vanishing question in L\^e's proposed comparison, in [preprint (2026), arXiv:2603.01219], under the hypothesis that the Bianchi-Massey tensor vanishes. The result applies to closed, connected, oriented manifolds with no upper dimension bound. We also extend Zhou's sphere-bundle formality criterion in [Algebr. Geom. Topol. 25 (2025), pp. 2297--2315] to two-stage oriented sphere bundles with positive odd fibre dimensions over a closed, connected, oriented, rationally formal base, provided that the second Euler class is pulled back from the original base. Their total spaces are rationally formal precisely when the Bianchi-Massey and normalized pentagonal tensors vanish. Our method develops the model-based strategy in Zhou's proof within a commutative bar-cobar framework, providing a starting point for constructing higher tensors and comparing them with higher-order formality obstructions.

entry.title: Classifying spaces of finite monoids with bounded homology
entry.content:
Floris Alderliefste

The classifying space BM of a monoid M is the geometric realization of the nerve of M, regarded as a category with one object; its fundamental group is the universal group U(M), the group generated by the elements of M with the multiplication table of M as relations. Let M be finite. We prove that if the integral homology of BM vanishes in all large degrees, then U(M) is trivial; more precisely, if a prime p divides the order of U(M), then H_k(BM; F_p) ≠ 0 for infinitely many k. It follows that three conditions on a finite monoid are equivalent: BM is homotopy equivalent to a finite CW complex; it is homotopy equivalent to a finite-dimensional one; its homology is bounded. In that case BM is simply connected. Together with a theorem of Ben-Bassat, that every finite simply connected CW complex is homotopy equivalent to BM for a finite monoid M, this determines these homotopy types: they are the finite simply connected complexes. A conjecture of the same paper, that every connected finite CW complex with finite fundamental group is of the form BM with M finite, is therefore false; the real projective plane is a counterexample. The proof compares the K-theory of BM with that of the classifying space of a finite group contained in M, through Atiyah's completion theorem. Two examples are worked out: a monoid with six elements whose classifying space is simply connected and has homology in every degree from 2 on (it is a wedge of spheres), and a monoid with 23 elements whose classifying space is the complex projective plane.

entry.title: The first L²-Betti number of aspherical manifolds and Poincaré duality groups of dimension at least three
entry.content:
Floris Alderliefste

The L²-Betti numbers b_p⁽²⁾ of a finite complex measure the square-summable harmonic p-chains on its universal cover. Singer's conjecture says that for a closed aspherical manifold of dimension n, one whose universal cover is contractible, they vanish outside the middle degree n/2. A manuscript of OpenAI dated 25 September 2026, released on 6 October 2026, proves the conjecture in dimension four; it is not refereed. Its proof assumes b₁⁽²⁾ > 0, builds from functions of finite energy on the fundamental group Γ a compact boundary on which Γ acts, and reaches a contradiction; dimension four enters only in a preliminary section. We show that the same argument gives b₁⁽²⁾ = b_{n−1}⁽²⁾ = 0 for every finite aspherical Poincaré complex of formal dimension n ≥ 3, hence for every closed aspherical topological manifold of dimension at least three (Theorem A), and for every finitely presented Poincaré duality group of dimension n ≥ 3 (Theorem B). To do so we state what Sections 3-10 of the manuscript prove as a criterion for groups (Theorem C): a finitely presented torsion-free group with one end, with H²(Γ; F₂Γ) = 0 and with no splitting over a finite or two-ended subgroup, has b₁⁽²⁾ = 0; and we prove, in every dimension n ≥ 3, the facts about Γ that the criterion needs. Theorems A and B depend on the manuscript's argument, which we cite and do not reproduce. One AI referee has followed that argument line by line and found no fault; no human has checked it, or this paper.

entry.title: An equivariant index theorem for the Heisenberg calculus
entry.content:
title: equivariant

Alexander Gorokhovsky, Erik van Erp

We derive a local fixed-point formula for the equivariant index of Heisenberg elliptic operators on closed contact manifolds equipped with an action of a compact Lie group preserving the contact form. The formula expresses the character of the equivariant index in terms of a cyclic-cohomological character of the noncommutative Heisenberg principal symbol. The main new ingredient is the construction of traces, one on each fixed-point set, defined by integration over twisted conjugacy classes in the Heisenberg group. The proof proceeds by a K-theoretic reduction to the equivariant index theorem of our paper "Toeplitz operators on contact manifolds and equivariant K-homology".

entry.title: An internal approach to symmetric monoidal $(\infty,n)$-categories
entry.content:
title: (infinity,n); abstract: cocartesian fibration

Arghan Dutta

We propose a definition of symmetric monoidal $(\infty,n)$-categories as special left double $(\infty,n)$-fibrations over the category of finite pointed sets. The definition makes sense in a general model of $(\infty,n)$-categories, under a mild condition on its discrete objects, and when the model is left proper and combinatorial we construct model structures whose fibrant objects are exactly these fibrations. For $n=1$ we show that the definition recovers Lurie's symmetric monoidal $(\infty,1)$-categories: the homotopy theory of special left double $(\infty,1)$-fibrations is equivalent to that of special coCartesian fibrations over the category of finite pointed sets. The equivalence is realized by an explicit Quillen equivalence, and two constructions, the staircase and coCartesian strings, translate between the two descriptions.

title: topos

Joseph Helfer, Patrick Lutz, Forte Shinko

We construct a topos for Borel mathematics: statements which are true in Borel mathemaics correspond in a precise way to statements which are true in the internal logic of this topos. We investigate several other properties of this topos, including proving that it satisfies a Borel analogue of the Church-Turing thesis: the statement that every function on a standard Borel space is Borel. We also show that an earlier construction of a similar "Borel topos" by van Osdol does not suit these purposes because of an error in that paper.

The positive-characteristic analogue of motivic cohomology with coefficients in an Anderson A-motive M over a function field of transcendence degree one was introduced in an earlier work of the author. entry.title: Hochschild operations and other invariants of stable equivalences of Morita type
entry.content:
abstract: algebraic k-theor

Shengyong Pan

We study stable equivalences defined by bimodule tensor identities over a commutative ring $R$. For the $R$-split exact structure, these identities preserve positive Hochschild homology and positive Hochschild cohomology with its cup product, Gerstenhaber bracket and, in prime characteristic, restricted power. A triangular comparison also identifies the relative singular Hochschild cochain complexes as $B_\infty$-algebras. For reduced pairs of finite-dimensional Frobenius algebras over an algebraically closed field, with diagonalizable Nakayama automorphisms, we construct compatible Frobenius functionals and compare the Tate--Hochschild BV operators in all degrees. For flat algebras over $R$ we give a Hochschild-cohomological criterion for comparing marked associative deformations. It applies to biadjoint Morita-type pairs and, by reduction, to all stable equivalences of Morita type between finite-dimensional algebras over any field. We compare the Bezrukavnikov--Ginzburg maps in characteristic zero by using a common triangular deformation or by lifting a two-sided tilting complex. We also compare marked module deformations over local Artin rings and their augmented universal rings. Further applications concern connected outer automorphism group schemes over perfect fields, the kernels of the quotient maps on ordinary algebraic $K$-theory, and the nonconnective $K$-theory of enhanced relative singularity categories. We construct biadjoint representatives over Henselian Noetherian local rings and relative stable tensor functors for almost $\nu$-stable derived equivalences. We also answer a question of Abe and Hoshino about preservation of the Gorenstein condition in a fixed codimension.

entry.title: Monadicity of noncommutative measurable spaces over $C^{\ast}$-algebras
entry.content:
abstract: presentable

Fosco Loregian, Antonio Lorenzin

In a recent paper, Tobias Fritz and the second author identified $\sigma C^*$-algebras as a tentative noncommutative analogue of measurable spaces. We advance this analogy by establishing monadicity of $\sigma C^*$-algebras over $C^*$-algebras and proving several results of interest to both the category theory and operator algebra communities. In detail, we show that: - The associated probabilistic morphisms, $\sigma$-cpu maps, admit a description via a comonad closely related to the Giry monad. Equivalently, $\sigma$-cpu maps can be characterized by a universal property. - The category of $\sigma C^*$-algebras and $\sigma$-homomorphisms is locally $\aleph_1$-presentable. - $\sigma C^*$-algebras have a tensor product induced by the maximal tensor product of $C^*$-algebras and satisfying an analogous universal property. - The notion of CP-instruments, defined as $\sigma$-additive assignments from a $\sigma$-algebra to a space of completely positive maps, can be adapted to this setting by taking as target the set of $\sigma$-normal completely positive maps between $\sigma C^*$-algebras. This yields a bijective correspondence with $\sigma$-cpu maps out of the tensor product of the previous item.

entry.title: Cup products with volume classes in bounded cohomology
entry.content:
Michelle Bucher, Roberto Frigerio

Let $M$ be a complete Riemannian $n$-manifold, $n\geq 2$, and suppose that either $M$ is negatively curved, or that it is a locally symmetric space of non-compact type. Via integration over straight simplices, every top-degree bounded differential form $\omega\in \Omega_b^n(M)$ defines a bounded cohomology class in $H^n_b(M)$. We prove that every such class belongs to the annihilator of the cup product in the whole graded algebra $H^{\geq 1}_b(M)$. In the case of closed orientable surfaces, this generalizes a result of Marasco, and, via transfer, provides a new proof of the fact that the cup product of the bounded Euler class of $SL(2,\mathbb{R})$ with itself vanishes. Our result also applies to degree-3 bounded classes constructed by Soma and Farre, thus showing that, for surface groups and for free groups, the annihilator of the cup product is infinite dimensional also in degree 3.

entry.title: Non-formality of prefactorization algebras

Coline Emprin, Alex Takeda

We construct a Poisson bracket on the cohomology of locally constant prefactorization algebras on $\mathbb{R}^m$ that provides an obstruction to formality in every dimension $m\geqslant 2$. Our construction combines colored obstruction sequences to formality with linking spheres and generalizes the two-dimensional bracket of Bruinsma, Schenkel, and Vicedo. We use it to extend their non-formality theorem for Lie algebra factorization envelopes to all higher dimensions. We also establish new non-formality results for factorization envelopes of Lie algebras, their compactifications and generalizations to $L_\infty$-algebras, free BF-type theories, higher abelian Chern-Simons theories and their compactifications.

entry.title: One monoid to realize them all: a master monoid for homotopy types
entry.content:
Isaac Carcac\'ia-Campos

Homotopy theory has traditionally been approached either through topological spaces or through categories of presheaves on suitable combinatorial categories, a perspective subsumed by Grothendieck's theory of test categories. In this paper, we develop a more algebraic viewpoint: homotopy types can be represented by actions of a single monoid on sets. This monoid is obtained by identifying all the objects of the semisimplicial category while retaining its face operators. Every CW homotopy type is the classifying space of the translation category of one of its actions, and its truncation at dimension n is finitely presented and realizes exactly the homotopy types of dimension at most n. The construction rests on a general result: every set-valued functor on a small category freely generates an action of its universal monoid, and its category of elements is a full coreflective subcategory of the resulting translation category. Hence every weak test category gives rise to a monoid whose actions realize all homotopy types; when the category has more than one object, however, this monoid is not itself a weak test category, so that a single monoid may realize all homotopy types without modelling homotopy theory as a localization. The obstruction lies in identifying objects, not in having a single one: there are strict test categories with a single object, such as the monoid of all self-maps of an infinite set and a countable monoid of primitive recursive functions.

entry.title: Second homotopy modules and infinite homotopy stable classes of four-manifolds
entry.content:
Tommy Hofmann, John Nicholson

We construct infinitely many closed oriented smooth 4-manifolds which are all stably diffeomorphic but pairwise not homotopy equivalent. Our examples are distinguished by their second homotopy modules, and provide the first examples which demonstrate that stable diffeomorphism does not determine the second homotopy module. They have fundamental group $(\mathbb{Z}/4)^4*\mathbb{Z}$ and arise as doubles of presentation 2-complexes. In contrast, we give criteria for isomorphism of second homotopy modules of doubles of 2-complexes, covering finite abelian, quaternion, dihedral and symmetric fundamental groups. We also establish non-injectivity of the doubling construction by showing that there exist homotopically distinct presentation 2-complexes over $Q_{28}$ whose doubles are homotopy equivalent.

Under a model combining uniform sampling on the manifold with uniform noise, we show that suitable choices of the radius and degree parameters recover the homotopy type of the underlying manifold with high probability. The analysis explains how the degree parameter suppresses sufficiently distant outliers while the radius scale captures topological signals. Our results provide theoretical support for the common intuition that degree bifiltrations carry meaningful topological information in the presence of noise.

entry.title: Exact, total and filtered small categories
entry.content:
Floris Alderliefste

For a non-empty connected small category we compare four properties: being filtered; exactness of colimits of abelian groups; Grothendieck's total asphericity, which says that colimits of simplicial sets over the category are homotopy colimits; and being quasi-filtered, which means that two arrows with a common source can be completed to a commutative square and that two parallel arrows are equalized by an integral combination of arrows whose coefficients sum to 1. Each implies the next. We give a category of finite ordered hypergraphs that is totally aspherical and whose colimits are exact over no non-zero ring, and we show that the category of finite ordered two-graphs (sets of triples that meet every four-element set in an even number of triples) is quasi-filtered and not totally aspherical. With the example of Isbell and Mitchell, the three implications are strict. A conjecture in Grothendieck's Les Dérivateurs, that totally aspherical categories are filtered, is therefore false; it holds for sifted categories, those over which colimits of sets commute with finite products.

entry.title: The profinite Grothendieck-Teichmüller monoid is a group, on a question of Lochak and Schneps
entry.content:
Floris Alderliefste

An element of the profinite Grothendieck-Teichmüller group $\widehat{\mathrm{GT}}$ of Drinfeld is a pair $(\lambda,f)$, with $\lambda$ a unit of $\widehat{\mathbb Z}$ and $f$ in the free profinite group $\widehat F_2$ on $x$ and $y$, that satisfies three relations and for which $x\mapsto x^\lambda$, $y\mapsto f^{-1}y^\lambda f$ is an automorphism of $\widehat F_2$. This article develops a second stage of an argument begun in 2013, revisiting Alain Badiou's use of topos theory in Being and Event and Logics of Worlds. The previous article diagnosed Badiou's reduction of topos theory to its atomistic, localic form as the scientific scapegoat in his attack on 'democratic materialism'. Now I ask what follows when this logicist illusion is dispelled and the categorical alternative is taken seriously, particularly with respect to forcing, semantic expression, and mathematical subjectification that constitute the key elements of Badiou's earlier work. In particular, I describe Cohen's forcing argument in the context of Grothendieck topoi and Kripke-Joyal semantics, thereby explicating the geometric structures implicit in Badiou's thinking. This reconstruction further brings into view a different way of understanding Badiou's concepts of subject, body, and change. Rather than treating a topos as merely a formal container for mathematical objects, I propose reading it as a body of mathematical expression, aligning with Johnstone's characterization of a topos as a 'universe of discourse'. At the same time, the geometrization of logic allows Badiou's own four-fold typology of change - when applied to topos theory itself as a mathematical 'event' - to be anchored to various historical definitions of a topos. In this way, the article bridges Badiou's two major works while clarifying how his own limited expression of mathematical formalism embodies his 'dialectical', ultimately singular concept of the event, and the way it clouds his philosophical understanding of locality and temporality.

We call $X$ Alexander formal if there are no such blocks at any root of unity, rationally, nor at the eigenvalue 1 modulo any prime $p$. Consequently, the strong formality of Kohno and Pajitnov implies formality of every finite abelian cover of $X$; the converse fails, through a Jordan block at an eigenvalue of infinite order, which no finite cover detects. Similarly, $A_\infty$-categories over $R$ are generalizations of $R$-linear categories in which composition of morphisms is only associative up to higher homotopies. Typically ${\mathscr F}(X,\omega)$ depends on many arbitrary choices. Hypergraphs are the natural language for group interactions, and topological data analysis has given us several ways to look at them: simplicial and cell complexes, persistent homology, and sheaves. All of these treat a hyperedge as an unordered set. In this paper, we introduce a different and, to our knowledge, new viewpoint that comes from Grothendieck's theory of dessins d'enfants and, unlike these approaches, takes into account the order in which vertices appear in each hyperedge and hyperedges appear around each vertex. A dessin is a bipartite graph drawn on a closed orientable surface. Through Walsh's classical correspondence between hypermaps and bipartite maps, every hypergraph equipped with a cyclic order of incidences at each vertex and inside each hyperedge is a dessin, and therefore determines a surface with faces and a genus. We develop this idea for temporal hypergraphs and build the surface by replaying history: incidences are added in the order in which they occurred, and each new incidence is inserted into the cyclic orders built so far, next to the earlier incidence to which it is related. We prove that every insertion either grows the hypergraph without creating a cycle, closes a cycle locally by splitting a face, or closes it globally by adding a handle; the number of independent cycles equals the number of local plus handle events, and the genus equals the number of handle events. These counts give interpretable, size-controlled measures of how a temporal hypergraph's cycles organize on a surface as it grows. We apply our method to five Stack Exchange communities and show that it separates communities that standard statistics cannot tell apart and quantifies how much the real order of interactions matters. We further discuss what the surface viewpoint adds to existing higher-order network analysis and how it opens a path toward dessin-based learning on hypergraphs.

Lurie's cobordism hypothesis classifies fully extended framed topological field theories valued in a symmetric monoidal $(\infty,n)$-category $\mathcal{C}$ with duals by the $\infty$-groupoid $\mathcal{C}^{\mathrm{fd}}$ of fully dualisable objects. This classification results in an $O(n)$-action on $\mathcal{C}^{\mathrm{fd}}$, where $O(n)$ acts on the framed bordism category by change of framing. Lurie observed that for a connective spectrum, this action is ``a version of the classical $J$-homomorphism.'' The sign (i.e.\ whether the action is $J_n$ or $\ominus J_n$) depends on the convention for the $O(n)$-action on framings, and is relevant for $\mathrm{pin}^\pm$ theories and hence for quantum systems with time-reversal symmetry. One of the best known invariants of multi-parameter persistent homology is the rank invariant, which is subsumed by the generalized rank invariant (GRI), obtained by naturally extending its domain. M\"obius inversion of the GRI not only provides a compact encoding of this invariant but is also useful for clarifying its relationship with other invariants of multi-parameter persistent homology. However, M\"obius inversion of the GRI has been defined only under suitable finiteness conditions on its domain and support. Namely, we formalize the notion of M\"obius invertibility, which captures when M\"obius inversion exists beyond these finiteness conditions, and investigate when the GRI is M\"obius invertible. In response to this higher-dimensional obstruction, we show that for finitely presentable $d$-parameter persistence modules, restricting the GRI to intervals subordinate to the finite grid supporting a minimal free presentation preserves its M\"obius inversion whenever the latter exists over all intervals. Since computing the GRI over all intervals in $\mathbb{R}^d$ is infeasible in practice, this result provides a principled justification for restricting the GRI to those intervals.

entry.title: On Tunnel Fusion and Yangian $R$-matrices
entry.content:
abstract: stable envelope

Dmitry Galakhov

XXX spin-chain Hamiltonians can be derived within the $R$-matrix formalism. For a simple Lie algebra $\mathfrak{g}$, the rational $R$-matrix $R$ intertwines the coproduct $\Delta$ in the Yangian $\mathsf{Y}(\mathfrak{g})$. $R$ admits a particular Gauss decomposition $R=LDU$, where the upper-triangular matrix $U$ can be obtained from the lower-triangular matrix $L$. We treat $U$ in three ways. Algebraically, $U$ is known as a factorization twist. It plays the role of a ``universalizer'': it conjugates a non-universal pseudo-coproduct $\mathscr{D}$ in the molten crystal chain basis to the true Yangian coproduct $\Delta=U^{-1}\mathscr{D} U$. Physically, $U$ can be obtained as a Berry phase in SUSY quiver QFT for a quiver associated with the Dynkin diagram of $\mathfrak{g}$. In this case, $U$ is calculated as a sum over tunneling amplitudes. Geometrically, $U$ can be interpreted as a renormalized Maulik-Okounkov stable envelope localized at a fixed point. In the physical setting, the Yang-Baxter equation (YBE), which ensures integrability, follows from the flatness of the Berry connection, which in turn follows from supersymmetry. However, the YBE imposes subtle constraints on the tunneling amplitudes, which we examine here. We construct recursion relations that allow higher collective amplitudes to be obtained from more elementary ones. We observe that different tunneling channels are in fact intertwined, leading to finer cancellations among amplitudes and to wall-crossing phenomena: depending on the parameters, the same amplitude is represented as a sum over different channels. We focus on $\mathsf{Y}(\mathfrak{sl}_2)$ with higher-spin and non-evaluation representations, as well as on the fundamental representation of $\mathsf{Y}(\mathfrak{sl}_{n+1})$.

entry.title: Asymptotic Dimension of Persistence Modules of Bounded Presentation
entry.content:
Sushovan Majhi, Atish Mitra, \v{Z}iga Virk

We compute the asymptotic dimension of spaces of multiparameter persistence modules of bounded presentation under the interleaving distance. The $d$-parameter modules with at most $n$ generators and $m$ relations have asymptotic dimension, and Assouad-Nagata dimension, exactly $d(n+m)$, the number of coordinates of their generator and relation grades, over every field; for two parameters this is $2(n+m)$. The space has continuous moduli, already for two parameters and $n,m\ge2$: over an infinite field it contains, at every scale, infinite uniformly separated families of pairwise non-isomorphic modules with one fibered barcode, so it is not doubling even at a fixed fibered barcode; already for $m\ge1$ it is not coarsely equivalent to a proper metric space. The proof is an induction on the number of distinct grade coordinates: an interleaving small compared with the gaps between these coordinates moves each of them by at most twice its size and preserves the induced grid representation, so the continuous moduli are invisible at large scale. Each class of modules at finite distance therefore embeds coarsely into Hilbert space; for $n,m\ge2$ over an uncountable field, the classes that contain these families admit no such embedding into a separable Hilbert space. Under the two-parameter matching distance $2(n+m)$ is a lower bound, attained for one generator and for two generators with at most one relation; on a finite net of $S$ slices the asymptotic dimension is at most $2nS$.

Hao Yu

Geometric chains are formal combinations of smooth maps from compact oriented manifolds or orbifolds with corners. In earlier work the author showed that, modulo a relation D that kills degenerate chains, they compute rational singular homology. We show that D can be replaced by a gluing relation, which identifies a chain with the sum of its restrictions to finitely many pieces whenever its source is glued from these pieces along whole codimension-one faces. With this relation the comparison map from singular homology is an isomorphism in all degrees for compact polyhedra and smooth manifolds without boundary, with rational and with integer coefficients. Unlike D, the gluing relation is defined through the sources alone, and chain-level identities such as the equivalence of a degree d covering with d times its base, which fails modulo D, and the correction terms of the chain map from a Morse complex, which are degenerate modulo D, become gluing relations. The proof is axiomatic; injectivity comes from integration or dual cells, surjectivity from cutting along regular levels, where the cut of a gluing relation is again one, and at the point we use Whitehead triangulations of manifolds with corners subordinate to their corner strata. The gluing relation, read on underlying spaces, also suffices for orbifold sources, with integer coefficients modulo classes with an orientation reversing automorphism, and for effective orbifold targets.

entry.title: Wasserstein Stability of the Nerve Map

Kenneth McCabe, Jose A. Perea

Given a locally finite open cover of a paracompact space, a subordinate partition of unity defines a map into the geometric realization of the nerve. When the cover is good, the nerve theorem asserts that this map is a homotopy equivalence. In applied topology, one specializes this construction to covers of metric data by open balls centered at finitely many landmarks. The corresponding nerve map represents the data inside the \v{C}ech complex, enabling one to pull cohomological or spectral invariants back to the data. Since point cloud data often comes equipped with weights encoding domain-specific importance, we introduce a weighted version of the nerve map and study its stability under perturbations of the landmarks and weights using metrics from optimal transport. Our main result is a Lipschitz stability theorem for the weighted nerve map under a uniform nondegeneracy assumption. We state the bound in terms of a scale-dependent optimal transport distance, and give an example where our estimate is attained. Since this distance is dominated by a multiple of the $1$-Wasserstein distance, Wasserstein stability follows as a corollary. We also give geometric conditions ensuring nondegeneracy, obtain explicit estimates of the Lipschitz constant for closed Riemannian manifolds, and sketch applications to Laplacian eigenvector cascading and Eilenberg--MacLane coordinates.

entry.title: Quantum-Information Probes of Collapse Dynamics in Causal Fermion Systems
entry.content:
abstract: covariance-spectr

Benjamin Kaminsky

Finster, Kleiner, and Paganini derived from causal fermion systems (CFS) a nonrelativistic effective collapse model whose statistical operator obeys, to leading order, a Kossakowski--Lindblad equation. In the factorized regime of that derivation, the dissipator is built from purely spatial operators $N_{k,a}$ with positive rates fixed by microscopic time-nonlocal kernels. We translate this CFS-specific generator into quantities accessible to coherent quantum processors. The resulting CFS Dirichlet form obeys an exact purity-loss identity under arbitrary Hamiltonian control, and its null algebra is the commutant of the $*$-algebra generated by the projected $N_{k,a}$. For joint eigenbranches we obtain an exact distinguishability functional controlling exponential coherence loss and a lower bound on channel distance from ideal unitary evolution. In an $n$-qubit dephasing sector, the projected kernels generate a positive-semidefinite covariance matrix $C$, with GHZ visibility $\exp[-2T\bm{1}^{\mathsf T}C\bm{1}]$. We prove that uniformly summable finite-range correlations yield at most $O(n)$ GHZ decay, whereas $O(n^2)$ scaling requires a collective non-summable component. Single- and two-qubit cat coherences reconstruct $C$, giving a covariance-spectroscopy protocol, while Knill--Laflamme conditions characterize first-order correctability of the projected CFS error algebra. We also derive an explicit compatibility inequality between macroscopic state reduction and long coherent computation and show why absence of probe heating does not imply absence of coherence signatures. The results do not exclude CFS: its covariance strength, $\ellmin$, and hardware projection remain underdetermined. They instead identify the microscopic input required for a genuine no-go theorem and establish scalable quantum processors as direct probes of the CFS collapse sector.

entry.title: Beyond the Lower-Star Filtration: Alternative Filtration Methods for Persistent Homology

In the lower-star filtration (LSF), simplices are assigned filtration values according to the maximum-vertex rule, with each simplex entering the filtration when its highest-valued vertex appears. A limitation of this construction is that some higher-dimensional simplices may enter simultaneously with their boundary faces, causing certain topological features to be filled immediately upon formation and thus not appear in the resulting persistence diagram. To address this limitation, we propose three alternative filtration methods: the \(\varepsilon\)-lower-star filtration (ELSF), the \(L_p\) filtration (LpF), and the softmax filtration (SMF). {ELSF introduces a dimension-dependent delay to the maximum-vertex rule,} allowing higher-dimensional simplices to enter the filtration after their boundary faces, whereas {LpF and SMF use aggregation functions that depend on all vertex values rather} than solely on their maximum. By modifying how filtration values are assigned, these methods allow simplices to enter the filtration more progressively, so that topological features such as loops and voids may persist over longer filtration intervals rather than being filled immediately. Consequently, the resulting persistence diagrams may include persistence features that are not observed under LSF, potentially providing useful information for distinguishing data populations. Experimental results on simulated and real-world datasets demonstrate that the proposed filtration methods are computationally efficient and can provide greater sensitivity to structural differences in the data than LSF.

Persistent Laplacians (PLs) address this limitation: for a pair of simplicial complexes in a filtration, the kernel of the persistent Laplacian recovers the persistent Betti number, while its non-zero spectrum carries additional geometric information. However, PLs are defined for individual pairs of filtration values, so analysing a whole filtration requires evaluating many operators that largely contain the same information, and the result is hard to summarize and interpret. In this paper, we show that this redundancy has a precise structure. For each pair of filtration values, we decompose the space of chains underlying the persistent up-Laplacian into the contributions inherited from the neighboring pairs and a remaining part, which we call the new persistent chain space. We show that the new persistent chain spaces of all earlier pairs form a direct sum decomposition of this space, so that every persistent up-Laplacian in the filtration is determined by them. Moreover, the new persistent chain spaces are non-trivial only at pairs given by the persistence pairing in the same and in the next homological dimension, so that the persistence pairing determines exactly where the persistent up-Laplacian can change. Experiments on several types of point clouds show that evaluating persistent Laplacians only at these pairs reduces the computation time, both for our implementation and for existing software.
